sentences.text: In 1972, Alberta implemented a policy of premium-free health care insurance coverage for all Alberta citizens over 65.

In 1998-99, Alberta Blue Cross coverage was available at no cost to Alberta seniors aged 65 and over, their spouses and dependents, and to widows and widowers aged 55 to 64 years receiving the Alberta Widows' Pension and their dependents.

In 1998-99, non-group coverage was also offered through the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan to residents under 65 who wished to obtain supplementary health care insurance through Alberta Blue Cross.

answer.text: In 1972, Alberta implemented a policy of premium-free health care insurance coverage for all Alberta citizens over 65. In 1998-99, Alberta Blue Cross coverage was available at no cost to Alberta seniors aged 65 and over, their spouses and dependents, and to widows and widowers aged 55 to 64 years receiving the Alberta Widows' Pension and their dependents. In 1998-99, non-group coverage was also offered through the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan to residents under 65 who wished to obtain supplementary health care insurance through Alberta Blue Cross.

unsupported.text: The Alberta Widows' Pension Program was introduced on May 1, 1983 to assist widows and widowers of limited income who were age 55 and older but under age 65, by providing financial, housing and health care benefits similar to those received by Alberta senior citizens, including premium-free coverage under the Basic Health Services Program, Extended Health Benefits Program and Alberta Blue Cross Non-Group Membership.

editorial_notes.reason: The cached answer pairs two different programs as if they were one, and cites a different page from the one the story pins.
editorial_notes.text: This answer was generated for a story question that assumed a change in coverage, and it is shown unedited. Its second and third sentences cite page 116 of the 1998-99 statistical supplement, not page 117, the page the story pins. Page 116 is the summary of Alberta Blue Cross non-group coverage: free for seniors 65 and over, their spouses and dependents, and some widows and widowers, available to residents under 65 as supplementary insurance, and covering items such as private or semi-private hospital accommodation, some prescription drugs and ambulance services. Page 117 counts who was enrolled in that program in 1998-99. Neither page describes the basic provincial plan the 1974 record refers to, so the answer's two halves do not describe the same program.
